selected.title: The Labeling Challenge
selected.audienceGap: Students assume any business-related task must belong to a specific degree type.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Realizes that tasks are often universal, not degree-exclusive.
selected.concept: Viewer is shown a task and challenged to assign it; discovery is that information is missing.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Viewer pauses before making snap judgments about degree contents.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

demonstration.input: A task description involving profit margin calculation.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Calculate margins. Degree: B.Com or BBA?
demonstration.observation: No supplied source connects this example to either category; the supported result is insufficient information.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What evidence would definitively link this task to one degree?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / three_column_audit; Connection = task_question_journal / peer_observation_journal; Discovery = insufficient_information / missing_evidence_reveal. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

hlni.insight: Tasks like margin calculation are not inherently exclusive to one degree without verified curriculum evidence.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume a degree label dictates the specific tasks within it.
hlni.viewerChange: Shifts from guessing based on labels to looking for evidence-based comparisons.
hlni.support: Logical reasoning: a single example without institutional context cannot define an entire category.
hlni.payoff: The viewer stops guessing and learns to investigate assessment criteria as the basis for comparison.

creativeAngle: Using a logical puzzle to expose the flaw in binary degree comparisons
objective: Guide students to identify missing evidence before making degree assumptions
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Snap Judgment
shots.visual: Close-up of a student holding two cards labeled B.Com and BBA, looking undecided.
shots.dialogue: B.Com or BBA? Choosing often feels like guessing.
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct eye contact, slightly skeptical expression.

shots.name: The Tension
shots.visual: Student stares at a laptop screen displaying a single task description.
shots.dialogue: We assume tasks fit one. Look at this.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Calculate margins. Degree: B.Com or BBA?
shots.cameraPerformance: Zoom in on the laptop screen.

shots.name: The Pause
shots.visual: Student pulls back, hand hovering over the keyboard, looking frustrated.
shots.dialogue: Is it simple? Let's check the evidence.
shots.cameraPerformance: Dynamic camera movement to show hesitation.

shots.name: The Method Reveal
shots.visual: Split screen: The task card on one side, an empty 'Source Link' box on the other.
shots.dialogue: Without a source linking it to curriculum, we cannot label it. Insufficient information.
shots.cameraPerformance: Pointing at the empty source box.

shots.name: The New Question
shots.visual: Student closes the laptop and writes a note in a journal.
shots.dialogue: Stop guessing. Ask: What evidence links this?
shots.onscreenText: What evidence would definitively link this task to one degree?

shots.name: The Purposeful Action
shots.visual: Student opens a real academic curriculum document to compare assessment criteria.
shots.dialogue: Compare actual assessment criteria, not just labels.

productionNotes.visualStyle: Clean, minimalist desk setup with clear graphic overlays.
productionNotes.performance: Conversational and inquisitive, avoiding salesy tones.
productionNotes.camera: Handheld for the hook, static for the analytical value section.
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts matched to the logical progression of the puzzle.
productionNotes.sound: Subtle ambient classroom noise, crisp voiceover.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Transform a binary degree choice into a logical puzzle that forces students to seek verifiable evidence.
shootingPriority: The student's reaction to the missing evidence
The final action of checking criteria
